title: SLA and Audit-Log Claim Library for Regulated Buyers
body:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact claim and contract language library for sales, solutions, and legal when engaging regulated customers (health, financial services, gov). It is intended to:
- Give concise, consistent one-liners for pitch decks and discovery calls.
- Provide technically accurate audit-log and data-handling language for SOW/SLA inserts.
- Map claims to SOC2 / ISO27001 / HIPAA control families so security reviewers can quickly validate equivalence.
- Surface common buyer objections and approved rebuttals.
Audience:
Sales Engineers, AEs, Solutions, Legal, Security/Privacy reviewers.
Status notes:
Draft: This is intentionally pragmatic and conservative. Language marked with [LEGAL REVIEW] should not be pasted into contracts without counsel sign-off.
High-level positioning (1-liners for marketing/sales)
- “Predictable, auditable inference: configurable audit logs, tamper-evident retention, and role-based access controls to meet SOC2 and HIPAA evidence needs.”
- "We keep customer request and inference metadata isolated and queryable for audits — no raw customer prompts are surfaced to non-authorized staff or analytics pipelines by default."
- "Redwood’s audit trail supports exportable, cryptographically hashed entries and per-tenant retention policies to align with customer compliance windows."
Short claim snippets (for slides / one-pagers)
- “Per-tenant, immutable audit logs (API request metadata, model version, response hash).”
- “Configurable retention windows: 30/90/365 days plus export on request.”
- "Audit records include: request id, timestamp, model variant, token counts, route/policy, and requestor identity when available."
Technical guardrails (what we actually do)
- Which events are logged: request metadata (headers, route, client id), model variant, model config (temperature, max tokens), duration and latency, success/error codes, token counts, and a response hash (SHA256). We do not store full unredacted customer PII unless customer enables deep logging for debugging and signs DPA addendum.
- Tamper-evidence: logs are write-once per shard with append-only semantics. Optional cryptographic hashes are available for tenant exports.
- Access controls: RBAC scoped by org and role; audit-log access is logged and requires privileged role.
- Retention controls: tenant-configurable retention, with secure deletion workflows that write a deletion event to the log.
Mapping to frameworks (quick crosswalk)
- SOC2 (Trust Services Criteria): Logging and monitoring -> we provide audit trail and monitoring hooks; Change management -> model rollout traces; Access controls -> RBAC for log access.
- ISO27001: A.12.4 (Event logging), A.12.5 (Control of operational software), A.9 (Access control) -> Redwood audit features support these by providing event capture, versioned model artifacts, and RBAC.
- HIPAA (Security Rule): Audit Controls (45 CFR §164.312(b)) -> we capture access and activity; Integrity (§164.312(c)(1)) -> tamper-evidence and hashes; Person or entity authentication (§164.312(d)) -> integration points with customer IdP for tenant user mapping.
Sample sales-verified claim language (short)
- “Redwood provides per-tenant audit logs capturing request id, timestamp, model id, token usage, and a SHA256 response fingerprint. Retention windows are configurable and governed by the customer’s tenancy settings.”
- "We support secure export of audit records for customer audits; optional signed hashes are available for exported archives."
Contract-ready sample clauses (for legal to iterate)
- Audit Log Delivery (SAMPLE) [LEGAL REVIEW]:
  "Provider shall maintain per-tenant immutable audit logs that capture request identifier, timestamp (UTC), model identifier and version, request route, token usage metrics, request and response metadata hashes, and the identity of the API credential or authenticated user. Customer may request an export of audit logs for the Term and for a period of up to X days following Termination. Provider shall deliver exported logs within 10 business days in a common format (JSON/CSV) and may redact customer-designated PII on export with prior notice."
- Retention & Deletion (SAMPLE) [LEGAL REVIEW]:
  "Customer may configure audit log retention via console or API to a minimum of 30 days and a maximum of 3,650 days (10 years) for enterprise plans. Upon deletion, Provider will mark entries as deleted, trigger secure overwrite per Provider policy, and emit a deletion event in the system audit trail."
- Incident Evidence Preservation (SAMPLE) [LEGAL REVIEW]:
  "Where Customer reasonably suspects a security incident, Provider will preserve relevant audit logs and model telemetry for up to 90 days while the incident is investigated, subject to scope and confidentiality constraints."
Notes on HIPAA-specific language:
- Avoid saying “we store PHI” — prefer “we process and log request metadata; customers control whether protected health information (PHI) is included in logged payloads via configuration and DPA options.”
- For healthcare buyers, emphasize: Private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), KMS/HSM key control, covered entity / business associate agreement (BAA) availability, and minimal default logging of prompt/response content.
Competitor differentiation (notes for value prop)
- Competitor A: logs everything by default (cheap UX) — risk: surfacing PHI and large egress for exports. Positioning: “Redwood defaults to metadata-first audit trails with explicit opt-in for deep payload capture.”
- Competitor B: audit logs are available but siloed in a separate analytics product with complex pricing. Positioning: “Audit trail is first-class, included in retention tiers; exports and signed-hash archives are straightforward.”
- Competitor C: limited cryptographic or tamper-evidence features. Positioning: "Offer signed export hashes and immutable, append-only retention as a differentiator for auditors."
Common buyer objections + suggested responses
- Objection: “We need full request/response capture for audits.”
  Response: "We can enable deep capture behind a contractually-scoped DPA addendum and store payloads in a tenant-isolated archive with configurable retention and export. Advise: consider token redaction and selective capture to reduce risk and cost."
- Objection: “How do we prove logs weren’t modified?”
  Response: "We provide optional signed-hash exports and an append-only log store; for Dedicated/Private customers we support additional cryptographic attestation workflows with HSM-backed keys."
- Objection: "Can we get raw logs in our SIEM?"
  Response: "Yes — direct S3 export or SIEM connector (Splunk/Datadog) is available on enterprise plans; exports can be signed and partitioned per customer."
Operational considerations for Solutions Engineers
- Demo checklist: show audit log UI, retention settings, role-based access page, and an export flow with signed-hash verification.
- Implementation notes: enable export S3 bucket in customer-managed account for highest compliance posture.
- For high-sensitivity customers: recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with customer-controlled KMS and disabled default payload logging.
Legal & privacy redlines to expect
- Buyers will ask to cap retention and force deletion semantics — be prepared to explain deletion vs. overwrite and how cryptographic hashes persist.
- Requests for continuous access to raw PHI logs will require a tailored BAA + SOC2 attestation window documentation.
Open questions / action items
- [ENG] finalize export-file-level signed-hash format and example verification script (owner: Jordan Patel).
- [SEC] produce a short whitepaper describing tamper-evidence model and append-only storage (owner: Evan Brooks).
- [LEGAL] review sample contract clauses and provide approved language variants for EU and APAC customers (owner: Priya Nair).
- [GTM] build a one-slide summary for AE playbook with three approved one-liners and a short demo script.
Appendix: quick checklist for sales call (scratchpad)
- Is the customer regulated (HIPAA/PCI/FINRA/etc)? If HIPAA, mention BAA availability and Private/Dedicated options up front.
- Confirm desired retention window and export frequency.
- Ask whether customer requires payload capture or metadata-only.
- Offer example SLA clause and note that legal will need to finalize the DPA.
- If buyer requests cryptographic attestation, flag to Solutions Eng + Security for pre-sale review.
Historical notes (why we keep this conservative)
- Customers care less about token-level metrics than coherent, exportable evidence that model routing and rollouts were applied. Auditors want: who, when, what model, and how long. Keeping default logs metadata-first reduces inadvertent PHI exposure and keeps cost predictable.
End of doc.
summary: Working library of approved sales and contract language for audit logs, retention, and SLA items mapped to SOC2/ISO/HIPAA. Includes sample clauses, objections, competitor callouts, and action items.
